newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - French stocks cautious, look to GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - French stocks cautious, look to GDP growth.

text.p: French stocks look set to end 1997 around current levels as investors wait and see if company profit forecasts reflect an improvement in gross domestic product, a Reuters poll of equity analysts showed on Wednesday.

The CAC-40 index is expected to end the year at around 2,700, according to an average of forecasts from six analysts, largely unchanged from the all-time closing high of 2,709.21 reached on March 10. On March 11, the last day of the poll, French stocks eased to 2,686.15.

Government predictions of an economic upturn have been bolstered by news of rising consumer spending and surveys showing that French industrialists are more optimistic about prospects for increased production.
But investors are still cautious, some wary that long-term interest rates could rise.
Nevertheless, the predictions of this survey are more bullish than those three months ago, when analysts expected the CAC-40 to reach only 2,400 by the end of 1997.
"Our target for 1997 is on the cautious side. We are still looking for changes in earnings forecasts. For next year, we expect a strong growth of GDP, we see it at three percent in 1998."
MICHELLE JARDIN, ANALYST, CREDIT LYONNAIS SECURITIES.
"We expect a rise, but a moderate one, because of the vulnerability of French long-term rates."
